description: Hand-curated ground truth for the support email classifier. Human-written emails, human-verified labels. No LLM-generated content. Edge cases deliberately included and tagged.

expected.summary: ideal one-sentence summary

schema.edge_case_types: optional list: ambiguous | short | typo | mixed_language | sarcasm

cases.input: Hi, I was charged twice for my subscription this month. My card was debited on both the 1st and the 3rd. Please refund the second charge.

expected.summary: Customer was charged twice for a subscription and requests a refund.

cases.notes: Canonical billing case; matches the few-shot example shape so the model is likely to get it right.

cases.input: I never received the invoice for last month. Can you send it again?

expected.summary: Customer requests a copy of last month's missing invoice.

cases.notes: Invoice delivery is billing, not technical, even though it sounds like delivery.

cases.input: Please cancel my subscription. I want to stop being billed from next month.

expected.summary: Customer wants to cancel their subscription and stop billing.

cases.notes: Ambiguity trap: 'cancel my subscription' could be read as account management, but the billing intent is explicit.

cases.input: Why did the price go up? My plan was $19 and now it says $25. I didn't agree to this.

expected.summary: Customer disputes an unagreed price increase on their plan.

cases.notes: Price-change dispute; tests whether the model understands it is a billing complaint, not a question.

cases.input: My paymnet was declined and now my account shows overdue. But I paid last week, I have the bank statement.

expected.summary: Customer says a payment that was declined is actually paid and disputes the overdue status.

cases.notes: Typo-rich email ('paymnet'); tests robustness to spelling errors and payment-status disputes.

cases.input: It has been 5 days since I requested a refund and I haven't heard anything. Status?

expected.summary: Customer follows up on a refund request made five days ago.

cases.notes: Refund follow-up; single clear intent.

cases.input: The promo code SUMMER2026 doesn't work at checkout. It says the code is invalid.

expected.summary: Customer reports a promo code is rejected at checkout.

cases.notes: Discount code issues belong to billing/pricing, not technical.

cases.input: I need to update the billing address on my account to the new office address.

expected.summary: Customer wants to update the billing address on their account.

cases.notes: Billing address vs account address distinction.

cases.input: My free trial ended yesterday but I was charged the full amount this morning. I only wanted to test the product, I wasn't ready to pay.

expected.summary: Customer was charged at trial end without intending to start a paid plan.

cases.notes: Trial-to-paid conversion dispute; tests billing intent without explicit refund request.

cases.input: I was charged in USD but I live in Europe. Can I pay in euros instead?

expected.summary: Customer asks whether they can be billed in euros instead of USD.

cases.notes: Currency question; billing intent hidden inside a question.

cases.input: Can you send me a receipt for my purchase on June 12th?

expected.summary: Customer requests a receipt for a June 12th purchase.

cases.notes: Simple receipt request.

cases.input: I cancelled my subscription last month and I'm STILL being charged. I have the cancellation confirmation email. This is theft.

expected.summary: Customer was charged after cancelling and cites their cancellation confirmation.

cases.notes: Emotional escalation plus a specific factual claim; summary must capture both the charge and the proof offered.

cases.input: Hello, our company received an overdue invoice from you but we never signed up for a paid plan. Please check.

expected.summary: Company disputes an overdue invoice for a plan they never signed up for.

cases.notes: B2B invoice dispute; no refund request, just a request to investigate.

cases.input: How much does the team plan cost per seat? We are a team of 12.

expected.summary: Customer asks about team plan pricing for a 12-person team.

cases.notes: Pricing question before purchase.

cases.input: Oh nice, another $49 mystery charge. I'm sure it's for something I definitely agreed to. Definitely. Surely my 'annual plan renewal' or whatever. Anyway, please fix it.

expected.summary: Sarcastic customer disputes an unexpected annual renewal charge.

cases.notes: Sarcasm must not be mistaken for general venting; the ask is still billing-related.

cases.input: The app crashes every time I try to upload a file. It worked yesterday. Error code UPL-2048.

expected.summary: Customer reports the app crashes during file upload with error UPL-2048.

cases.notes: Canonical technical case; mirrors a few-shot example.

cases.input: I get 'Invalid credentials' when I try to log in, but my password is definitely correct.

expected.summary: Customer cannot log in and sees an invalid credentials error despite a correct password.

cases.notes: Login failure; technical even though it involves an account, because the ask is about a malfunction.

cases.input: Everything is so slow lately. Loading a dashboard takes 20 seconds.

expected.summary: Customer reports severe performance problems loading the dashboard.

cases.notes: Performance complaint; minimal detail.

cases.input: After the latest update, the export button does nothing. I click it and nothing happens. No error, no file.

expected.summary: Customer reports the export button stopped working after the latest update.

cases.notes: Regression-style bug report tied to a version update; the kind of case this system must catch.

cases.input: The error message says 'Unexpected token Z in JSON at position 4'. I have no idea what that means and neither does my IT guy.

expected.summary: Customer reports an incomprehensible technical error message and wants help.

cases.notes: Raw developer error message pasted by a non-technical user; summary must reflect confusion.

cases.input: I lost three weeks of data when the sync failed. Is there any way to recover it?

expected.summary: Customer reports losing three weeks of data after a sync failure and asks about recovery.

cases.notes: High-stakes data loss; the emotional weight must not change the classification.

cases.input: Our integration with your API started returning 500s this morning. We have a script that polls it hourly.

expected.summary: Customer reports their API integration returns 500 errors since this morning.

cases.notes: B2B technical case with an exact symptom window.

cases.input: The mobile app doesn't sync with my desktop. Changes on the phone never show up on the laptop.

expected.summary: Customer reports mobile app changes do not sync to the desktop app.

cases.notes: Sync complaint across devices.

cases.input: Exporting my report to PDF fails every time. It works for CSV though.

expected.summary: Customer reports PDF export fails while CSV export works.

cases.notes: Format-specific failure narrows the diagnosis; tests precision in the summary.

cases.input: I keep getting logged out randomly in the middle of work. It happened 4 times today.

expected.summary: Customer reports being randomly logged out four times in one day.

cases.notes: Session issue; technical malfunction, not an account access request.

cases.input: I signed up two days ago and I haven't received a single email from you. Not the welcome, not the confirmation.

expected.summary: Customer reports not receiving any emails since signing up two days ago.

cases.notes: Email delivery is technical; easy to mislabel as billing (invoice-related).

cases.input: The video won't load in my browser. It just shows a black screen with a spinner.

expected.summary: Customer reports a video that will not load and shows a black screen.

cases.notes: Media playback failure.

cases.input: Since the update on Monday, the whole app is just a white screen. I tried clearing the cache.

expected.summary: Customer reports a white screen after Monday's update despite clearing the cache.

cases.notes: Blank-screen regression after an update; customer already tried a workaround.

cases.input: It works in Chrome on my laptop but the desktop app shows an error every time I open a project.

expected.summary: Customer reports project errors in the desktop app while Chrome works.

cases.notes: Platform-specific failure requires careful summary; easy to overgeneralize.

cases.input: It's broken. Please fix.

expected.summary: Customer reports something is broken without providing details.

cases.notes: Extremely short and vague; classification must not fail, the summary should flag the missing detail.

cases.input: I forgot my password and can't get into my account.

expected.summary: Customer forgot their password and cannot access their account.

cases.notes: Canonical account case; also appears in few-shot examples.

cases.input: Please update the email address on my account from the old one to newmail@example.com.

expected.summary: Customer wants the email address on their account updated.

cases.notes: Profile change request.

cases.input: I want to delete my account and all the data in it.

expected.summary: Customer requests full account deletion including their data.

cases.notes: Account deletion is account, not billing, even if it ends billing too.

cases.input: I lost my phone and the authenticator app with it. I can't get the 2FA code anymore. My account is locked out.

expected.summary: Customer lost their 2FA device and is locked out of their account.

cases.notes: 2FA lockout; high friction, high stakes.

cases.input: My account got locked after too many wrong password attempts. Can you unlock it?

expected.summary: Customer's account was locked after failed login attempts and wants it unlocked.

cases.notes: Locked-account recovery; account even though it started with login attempts.

cases.input: How do I change my username? I picked something stupid years ago.

expected.summary: Customer asks how to change their username.

cases.notes: Simple profile question.

cases.input: Please add a new teammate to our workspace. Her email is jane@ourcompany.com and she needs editor access.

expected.summary: Customer requests a new teammate be added to the workspace with editor access.

cases.notes: Workspace administration is account management, not billing.

cases.input: Someone logged into my account from a different country. I changed my password but I'm worried. Please check for suspicious activity.

expected.summary: Customer suspects unauthorized access from another country and asks for an account check.

cases.notes: Security concern; must not be downgraded to a generic password question.

cases.input: I have two accounts and I'd like to merge them into one. Is that possible?

expected.summary: Customer asks whether their two accounts can be merged.

cases.notes: Uncommon request; tests the model against a request it has never seen.

cases.input: Our company rebranded. Can you change the company name shown on our account?

expected.summary: Customer wants the company name on their account updated after a rebrand.

cases.notes: Profile update at company level.

cases.input: I want to close my account entirely. What happens to my remaining subscription credits?

expected.summary: Customer wants to close their account and asks what happens to unused credits.

cases.notes: Deliberate ambiguity: account closure with a billing question embedded; the primary ask is account closure.

cases.input: Why can't I see the admin settings? I'm the owner of the workspace.

expected.summary: Workspace owner asks why they cannot access admin settings.

cases.notes: Permissions question; account-level, not a technical error.

cases.input: I deactivated my account for the summer and now I want it back. All my data still there?

expected.summary: Customer wants their deactivated account reactivated and asks if their data remains.

cases.notes: Reactivation flow with a data question.

cases.input: I need a copy of all my personal data for a GDPR request.

expected.summary: Customer requests a copy of their personal data under GDPR.

cases.notes: Data export for privacy rights; account/privacy domain.

cases.input: Please make me an admin on our team account. My colleague is the owner.

expected.summary: Customer asks to be made an admin on their team account.

cases.notes: Role change request.

cases.input: It would be great if you added dark mode. Half of our team works at night.

expected.summary: Customer requests a dark mode feature for night-time work.

cases.notes: Feature request; no malfunction, no billing, no account change.

cases.input: Hello, we are an analytics company and we'd love to discuss a partnership with you. Who should we talk to?

expected.summary: Company proposes a partnership and asks for the right contact.

cases.notes: Partnership inquiry; general business outreach.

cases.input: Yeah the app is great. Really. The design, the speed, everything is absolutely perfect. Why would anyone ever want a dark mode? Anyway, back to my issue: the search in my inbox is completely broken and has been for a week.

expected.summary: Sarcastic customer reports inbox search has been broken for a week.

cases.notes: Heavy sarcasm wrapping a real bug report; the actionable ask is technical.

cases.input: Hola, escribo desde España. Mi factura de julio no me ha llegado y necesito una copia. Muchas gracias.

expected.summary: Spanish-speaking customer requests a copy of their missing July invoice.

cases.notes: Mixed-language email (Spanish with an English domain context); must classify by content, not language.

cases.input: hi

expected.summary: Customer sent only a greeting with no request.

cases.notes: Extremely short edge case; nothing actionable, must not guess a category.

cases.input: The new dashboard layout is confusing. I can't find where my reports went. Other people on my team agree.

expected.summary: Customer gives feedback that the new dashboard layout is confusing.

cases.notes: UX feedback; not a technical malfunction, no direct request.

cases.input: Hi, I'm a student researching AI tools for a university paper. Could I interview someone on your team for 20 minutes?

expected.summary: Student requests an interview with the team for a university research paper.

cases.notes: Research request; clearly general.

cases.input: Just wanted to say the support team is amazing. You helped me last week and everything works now. Thanks!

expected.summary: Customer thanks the support team for resolving their issue last week.

cases.notes: Pure compliment; no action needed, must not invent a category.

cases.input: What's on your roadmap for this year? We're deciding whether to commit to your tool long-term.

expected.summary: Prospective long-term customer asks about this year's product roadmap.

cases.notes: Roadmap question with buying intent; still general information, not billing.

cases.input: Honestly I don't understand what your product does. I signed up after an ad but nothing makes sense.

expected.summary: Customer is confused about what the product does after signing up.

cases.notes: Product confusion; not technical (nothing malfunctioning) and not account (no access issue).

cases.input: Your competitor's tool does everything you do for half the price. Should I just switch?

expected.summary: Customer compares the product unfavorably to a competitor and questions whether to switch.

cases.notes: Competitor comparison; not a billing complaint even though pricing is mentioned.

cases.input: Do you have an office in Berlin? My team is looking for local vendors.

expected.summary: Customer asks whether the company has a Berlin office.

cases.notes: Unrelated company question.

cases.input: Wishing everyone a great holiday season! Thanks for a good year.

expected.summary: Customer sends seasonal greetings and thanks.

cases.notes: Holiday greeting; must not be misread as account or billing.

cases.input: I have been with you for three years and I have NEVER seen such terrible support. Do better. That is all.

expected.summary: Long-term customer complains about support quality without a specific request.

cases.notes: Pure venting with no actionable ask; summary must state the complaint and the absence of a request.

cases.input: Hi, I'm a journalist from TechDaily covering AI startups. Could we get a comment or a quote from your CEO for a story?

expected.summary: Journalist requests a comment from the CEO for a TechDaily article.

cases.notes: Press inquiry; general outreach.

cases.input: Can you tell me what time it is in Shanghai?

expected.summary: Customer asks an unrelated factual question.

cases.notes: Deliberately unrelated; also present in the v2 few-shot examples to reinforce the general fallback.

cases.input: My subscription renews tomorrow but I want to change it to the yearly plan first. Is that possible before the renewal?

expected.summary: Customer wants to switch to the yearly plan before tomorrow's renewal.

cases.notes: Plan change timed against a renewal; billing, but tests timing comprehension.

cases.input: My card keeps getting declined at checkout but my bank says the card is fine. The error message says 'payment declined - invalid merchant configuration'. Help?

expected.summary: Customer reports card declines at checkout despite the bank confirming the card is fine.

cases.notes: Splits the difference between billing (payment failure) and technical (config error message); billing wins because the pain point is the charge.

cases.input: My password stopped working out of nowhere. I didn't change it. Did you disable my account?

expected.summary: Customer cannot log in with a password that stopped working and fears their account was disabled.

cases.notes: Sits between technical (login malfunction) and account (access); the fear of a disabled account makes account the right call.

cases.input: plese fix my acount. its bin locking me out every day since the last update. this is the 5th time now.

expected.summary: Customer reports their account has locked them out daily since the last update.

cases.notes: Multiple typos plus a technical trigger ('since the last update') wrapping an account access problem.

cases.input: Bonjour, je ne peux plus me connecter a mon compte depuis ce matin. It worked fine yesterday. Merci de m'aider.

expected.summary: French-speaking customer reports being unable to log in since this morning.

cases.notes: Mixed French/English; login malfunction is technical per the category definitions, even though it involves an account.

cases.input: Help me. My email.

expected.summary: Customer sent an incomplete message about their email with no clear request.

cases.notes: Too incomplete to classify; must fall back to general rather than guess account or technical.

cases.input: Oh sure, lock me out again. I'm SURE it's for my own safety. I love the 'security'. Anyway, can I get back in or should I just start a new account?

expected.summary: Sarcastic customer asks to regain access after being locked out.

cases.notes: Sarcasm wraps a real access request; summary must capture the ask, not the tone.

cases.input: Ai un problema con mi factura, me cobraron dos veces este mes. Pls send the money back. Thx.

expected.summary: Spanish-speaking customer reports a double charge and requests a refund.

cases.notes: Mixed Spanish/English plus informal abbreviations; double charge + refund request is billing.

cases.input: I don't want to pay for this anymore. What are my options?

expected.summary: Customer wants to stop paying and asks what options exist.

cases.notes: Ambiguous between billing (stop paying) and general (open question); the explicit refusal to pay points to billing.

cases.input: UNSUBSCRIBE

expected.summary: Customer unsubscribes from emails.

cases.notes: One word, all caps; an email-preference request that belongs to none of the support categories and must not become account.

cases.input: Stop charging me. I deleted my account months ago and you still take money from my card every month.

expected.summary: Customer is still being charged after deleting their account months ago.

cases.notes: Deliberate ambiguity: account deletion vs continued billing; the active ask is to stop charges, so billing.
